label: token right after an early "u" (t=1 or 2)
explanation: Fires in the original phase on the step immediately after the letter u was input, but only when that u is at position 0 or 1 (so the active step is t=1 or t=2). It fires on essentially every such step regardless of the current input token. Magnitude is highest when u is the very first token (t=1, ~2.87 max), and weaker (~0.55-0.75 of max) when u is at position 1 (t=2). A few weak activations occur at t=3 after u at position 2. It does not fire after u later in the sequence, after any other letter, at the delimiter, or during the copy phase.

issues: Minor: the claim that it 'does not fire in the copy phase' is not strictly true. There are 3 copy-phase activations on dev (t=5, L=3, right after u is fed back as an output, value about 0.02). This is negligible.

The 233 test misses are almost all at t=3 right after a u at position 2, with values from 0.00 to 0.03 of max. They hold 0.0% of activation mass, which matches the 'small weak tail' the explanation describes. It is not a systematic gap worth adding to the predicate.
The predicate has no false positives on test (precision 1.0), so it fires on every step after an early u, whatever the input token is.
